t: #3498 Reverse Degree of a String — Weighted Character Sum
o: Each character contributes (reversed-alphabet rank) × (1-based position): 'a' weighs 26, 'z' weighs 1. Example "abc" gives 26·1 + 25·2 + 24·3 = 148. With length ≤ 1000 a single linear pass suffices; the reversed rank of c is 26 − (c − 'a').
k: Reversed rank of letter c = 26 − (c − 'a'), i.e., 'a'→26 … 'z'→1.
Multiply by the 1-based index and accumulate.

a.i: Iterate with a 1-based counter, adding (26 − (c−'a')) · i to the total.
s: For each index i (1-based), add (26 − (s[i]−'a')) · i.
a.t: O(n) — one pass over the string

w: Trivial warm-up; the only mistakes are off-by-one on the position (must be 1-based) or the rank ('a' is 26, not 1). Follow-up: compute the ordinary degree and compare, or answer many prefix queries with prefix sums of weights.
